evals.prompt: Write a Sabbath School lesson on the call of Abraham, Genesis 12. For an adult class, teaching Sabbath 2026-08-15. English.
evals.expected_output: This asks for something Sabbath School does not do. The lesson for any Sabbath is set by the quarterly Adult Bible Study Guide and used church-wide, so there is no original lesson to write and no theme to accept. The correct response does NOT produce a seven-day lesson on Genesis 12. It says in a sentence or two that Sabbath School follows the quarterly, works out which lesson actually falls on Sabbath 2026-08-15 (Q3 2026 began June 27, so the lesson taught on a given Sabbath is the one whose printed date range ends the day before), and offers to build the teacher's guide for that lesson. If the user genuinely wants an original study of Genesis 12 rather than the quarterly lesson, it points them at bible-study-deep instead.
expectations: Does NOT write an original seven-day lesson, Sabbath Afternoon through Friday
Does NOT accept 'the call of Abraham' as a theme to build a lesson around
States that Sabbath School follows the quarterly Adult Bible Study Guide, set church-wide
Works out, or offers to work out, which quarterly lesson falls on Sabbath 2026-08-15
Shows awareness that a lesson is taught on the Sabbath AFTER its printed date range ends
Offers to build a teacher's guide for that lesson once the official text is in hand
Redirects to bible-study-deep if the user actually wants passage-driven exegesis of Genesis 12
Does not invent quarterly content, daily section titles, or a Memory Text
Asks for the output language rather than assuming it

evals.prompt: Saya mengajar Sekolah Sabat pekan ini. Pelajaran 6 kuartal ketiga 2026. Tolong buatkan penuntun guru.
evals.expected_output: The core case. Locate Q3 2026 lesson 6, get the official text (ssnet.org, absg.adventist.org, or ask for a paste), then build teachers-guide.md and teachers-guide.html in Indonesian: eight numbered sections, Appendix A with every Bible text in Terjemahan Baru, Appendix B as source apparatus, ledger in the markdown only. Quotes sit in the day they explain, all of them, never piled in an appendix. Verse references are clickable and open embedded TB text.
expectations: Does NOT reconstruct the lesson from its number or the quarter theme
Attempts to locate the official text, naming real sources (ssnet.org, absg.adventist.org, divisional PDF)
If the lesson cannot be read, says so in one short sentence and asks the user to paste it
Names precisely what is needed: title, Ayat Hafalan, reading list, five daily titles with passages, Friday discussion questions
Counts the Friday discussion questions rather than assuming three
Output in Indonesian using quarterly labels: Sabat Sore, Ayat Hafalan, Pendalaman, Pertanyaan Diskusi
Eight numbered sections in order, then Appendix A, Appendix B
Every day in the day-by-day map carries its own quotes: EGW, SDABC, commentary, all that bear on that day, not one token quote
Ellen G. White quotes are gold-chipped; SDABC and other commentary are neutral; verbatim and paraphrase are visibly distinguished
Every English quotation has an Indonesian pane labelled a working translation, not presented as the quotation
Timed plan minutes are contiguous, sum to the stated total, and assign all five days to a block
Application survives compression; the survey block is what gets cut
teachers-guide.html rendered from references/teachers-guide-template.html
No ledger, no para_id, no provenance tags in the HTML; all retained in the markdown
Verse references clickable, data-ref carries the full canonical reference including book name
Comma-continued references like '14:5, 13, 26, 27' resolve as four verses in one popup, with verse numbers shown
EGW further-reading links point at the website, never a PDF, with book numbers verified

evals.prompt: I need a Sabbath School lesson on the state of the dead for a class that has three or four non-Adventist visitors most weeks. 30 minutes only, and one of our members always brings up near-death experiences.
evals.expected_output: Another request framed as a topic rather than a quarterly week. Same correction as eval 1: no original lesson gets written. The response asks which Sabbath is being taught so the quarterly lesson can be found, while capturing the genuinely useful details the user volunteered (visitors present, 30 minutes, the predicted near-death-experience objection) because those shape the guide once the lesson is known. If the quarterly week that Sabbath does touch the state of the dead, the guide engages the distinctive directly without softening it for visitors, defines terms on first use, and prepares an honest scriptural answer to the near-death-experience question with a time-box.
expectations: Does NOT write an original lesson on the state of the dead
Asks which Sabbath is being taught so the quarterly lesson can be identified
Retains the volunteered details for later use: visitors present, 30 minutes, the near-death-experience objection
Explains briefly why a theme cannot be chosen, without lecturing
Plans the 30-minute compression explicitly once it has a lesson, cutting the survey block rather than the application
Anticipates the near-death-experience objection by name and answers it from Scripture with a time-box
For visitors: defines terms on first use and stages no question where a visitor's honest answer is publicly wrong
Does not soften an Adventist distinctive because visitors are present
Offers bible-study-deep if the user wants a passage study on the state of the dead independent of the quarterly
